The rule: a tenant must not paint a wall on a day if there is no approval of that tenant on or before that day. For Ben on 7 January 2027, an approval happened on 5 January 2027, which is no later than 7 January. So the condition for the prohibition ("it is not the case that there is an approval...") is false, and the prohibition does not apply. The text then says nothing further about whether painting is permitted or required on that day; it simply doesn't forbid it. Of the options, "permitted, and the text does not say whether it is required" fits best, since the absence of a prohibition leaves painting permitted, while nothing makes it required.

ANSWER: D
